# Font gap — the 36-template Khmer event pack (TP-2.2, 2026-10-25)

The pack asks for 14 families (`template-pack/fonts.json`). The app's typography registry ships four self-hosted
OFL faces and three system fallbacks (`docs/typography-contract.json`, `src/js/typography-contract.js`). This note
records, role by role, whether the requested family exists, and which action was taken. The substitution rule
(TP-OD-1) is the one that applies: no font file was added for this order.

## Registry as shipped

| id | family | bundled | scripts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `noto-sans` | EInvite Noto Sans | yes (`assets/fonts/noto-sans-latin-*.woff2`) | Latin, Khmer fallback |
| `noto-serif` | EInvite Noto Serif | yes (`assets/fonts/noto-serif-latin-*.woff2`) | Latin, Khmer fallback |
| `noto-sans-khmer` | EInvite Noto Sans Khmer | yes (`assets/fonts/noto-sans-khmer-*.woff2`) | Khmer, Latin fallback |
| `noto-serif-khmer` | EInvite Noto Serif Khmer | yes (`assets/fonts/noto-serif-khmer-*.woff2`) | Khmer, Latin fallback |
| `serif-georgia`, `sans-arial`, `sans-trebuchet` | system faces | no | Latin, Khmer fallback |

`@font-face` rules live in `src/css/bundle-account.css` and are loaded by every authenticated route. Khmer faces
declare `unicode-range: U+1780-17FF, U+19E0-19FF` and a `size-adjust`/ascent override pair, so Khmer glyphs come from
the bundled WOFF2, never from an operating-system face.

## Why the substitution path

TP-OD-1 permits adding a self-hosted OFL WOFF2 per missing family. Twelve families are missing. Adding them would
mean, for each face: a subset WOFF2, `assetSha256` and `licenseFile` entries in the generated typography contract,
an upload/strict-boundary allow-list update, a licence row in `docs/FONT_LICENSES_AND_REGISTRY.md`, and new
`@font-face` rules loaded lazily on the pack path. That is a typography-contract change (model, hostile-input,
offline, shaping and export tests) rather than a template-pack integration, and the order's decision 7 says not to
build a new app feature for this order. The work order's own fallback is explicit: when a family cannot be added
within the order's budgets, `substitute the nearest registry family, list it in
docs/templates/FONT-SUBSTITUTIONS.md, and continue`. This file and `FONT-SUBSTITUTIONS.md` are that record.

The visible consequence is honest: the pack's ceremonial Moul / festive Koulen display faces and its script names
render in Noto Serif Khmer / Noto Sans Khmer / Noto Serif. Layout, hierarchy, contrast and Khmer shaping hold, and
the acceptance run measured **zero** text overflow after the converter's fit/height correction. The owner can
close the gap later under TP-OD-1 without touching the templates: replace the family in `FONT_ROLES`
(`tools/build-template-pack.py`), rebuild, and re-run the acceptance harness.

## Proof obligations (TP-2.2)

| check | evidence |
|---|---|
| Zero third-party requests on the editor, a pack template and the public page | `artifacts/next-work/review-tp/tp-2-2-network.json` |
| Each used face reports `loaded` in `document.fonts` | same file, `fonts` array |
| Khmer glyphs render from the bundled face | `CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode` rows in the same file |
| Editor route bytes unchanged by the pack | TP-1.5 ledger line (`bundle-index.js` 1 097 217 B before and after) |
| CSP clean | `tools/run-gates.py --phase csp` / `CSP_CHECK_PASSED` |
